title: tine monitor ... --json
description: Inline monitor verdicts and stop tokens. `stop`/`stops` list signed stop tokens (claim convention `opentine.monitor-stop/1`, held and never released); `verdicts` lists held monitor verdicts (`opentine.monitor-verdict/1`) and whether each signer is a pinned monitor key; `verify` checks offline that every blocked or replaced action in the given runs has its verdict. `fail:` findings block; `advisory:` findings block only with `--strict`. `backtest` replays recorded trajectories against a rule monitor and reports, per reasoning-visibility group (never pooled across groups), catch rate on attack-labelled trajectories and false-positive rate on benign ones, for the replay and for the recorded online verdicts. Online verdicts that saw another reasoning visibility or another input are counted, not compared. A verdict from the same monitor digest must reproduce byte for byte (`bit_identical`); `diff` lists every compared step whose action or decision changed. `collusion` compares an untrusted monitor's catch rate on attacks that carry a coordination signal with those that do not; its findings are advisory only (D12) and `ok` is always true. `protocol-sign` signs an `opentine.collusion-protocol/1` manifest that commits to a secret seed; `protocol-run` verifies it against the pinned roles (a `policy` key, never an `optimizer` key; refused when unpinned), checks the revealed seed, applies the paraphrase, re-sampling, honeypot, cross-monitor disagreement and steganography probes over seeded trials and reports flagged-trial rates with Wilson and Clopper-Pearson intervals; `ok` is false only when the signed manifest sets `required` and the monitor does not clear. `run` evaluates an ingest stream and writes coverage records (`opentine.monitor-coverage/1`); `heartbeat` signs one heartbeat (`opentine.monitor-heartbeat/1`); `coverage` reports the proven fraction of captured events a monitor evaluated; `validate` signs an operating point (`opentine.monitor-operating-point/1`); `suspicion` lists cumulative-suspicion and doom-loop flags.
